items.name: Ancient City of Ephesus
items.summary: A Roman port city whose processional way leads past the Library of Celsus, Hadrian’s Temple and the terrace houses.

image.alt: The two-storey marble façade of the Library of Celsus at Ephesus
image.credit: Emre D. / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 4.0

items.name: Temple of Artemis (Artemision)
items.summary: A single re-erected column marks one of the ancient world’s great sanctuaries, once counted among the Seven Wonders.

image.alt: A lone re-erected column standing in the marshy field of the Artemision
image.credit: Roy Egloff / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 4.0

items.name: Ayasuluk Hill & Basilica of St John
items.summary: Remains of a great early Christian basilica sit below the medieval fortress that overlooks today’s town.

image.alt: Columns and brick walls of the Basilica of St John on Ayasuluk Hill
image.credit: Giorgio Galeotti / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 4.0

items.name: İsa Bey Mosque
items.summary: A fourteenth-century mosque at the foot of Ayasuluk Hill, marking the arrival of Turkish principalities in the valley.

image.alt: Stone façade and minaret of the İsa Bey Mosque in Selçuk
image.credit: Giorgio Galeotti / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 4.0

items.name: Ephesus Museum
items.summary: Finds from Ephesus and the Artemision, including statues of Ephesian Artemis, shown in themed halls in the town centre.

image.alt: Marble statue of Ephesian Artemis displayed in the Ephesus Museum
image.credit: Furkan Akkurt / Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 4.0

items.name: Şirince village
items.summary: A hillside neighbourhood of stone houses, fruit wines and olive groves, named a Best Tourism Village by UN Tourism in 2023.

image.alt: Whitewashed houses with tiled roofs spread across a green hillside in Şirince
